nipo.vintage_label: Global Trade Alert, New Industrial Policy Observatory, October 2026 extract (as of 5 October 2026)
nipo.staged_d: Global Trade Alert's measures are not yet matched to the six supply-chain stages, so they are counted for the whole economy and not listed by sector.
nipo.strength_words: Strength scores a measure by the bite of its instrument (a grant, loan, local-content rule or import ban counts more than monitoring), whether Global Trade Alert judges it to favour domestic firms, how widely it applies (a whole sector counts more than one named firm) and the money or trade it covers; measures that are part of a package of several instrument types count up to 60% more. In this run half of the measures with a positive strength score between 0.40 and 0.75; the strongest scores 2.15.
nipo.confidence_words: Mapping confidence says how firmly the measure's product list and text tie it to energy sectors (averaged over the sectors it maps to): 0.10 when none of its listed products are energy-sector goods, 0.25 for a measure without a product list, from 0.75 up when its products fall in these sectors, and up to 2 when its title, source and Global Trade Alert's sector flags corroborate the mapping.

caveats.text: Scores compare Kosovo with other economies in the same sector; they are not measures of risk or profit in absolute terms.
All index values are the NEIS baseline as of 30 October 2026, scored at six supply-chain stages; Strategic Insights recomputes them under other weightings.
Some of Kosovo's sectors are not placed: a score is compared with other economies only when the economy is sovereign and at most half of the score rests on filled-in data.
Some figures behind these scores are filled in where the source has no value: with zero where a source lists every holder, otherwise with the world average.
Kosovo has no Strategic Index because it has no International Energy Agency Policies and Measures records.
